This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Video Conferencing/Physical Mode).
This is an application for bail.

The appellant-petitioner has been convicted for the offences under sections 451/506 (Part-II) of the Indian Penal Code and section 8 of the POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of two years and to pay a fine of Rs.2,000/- (rupees two thousand) and in default, to undergo further rigorous imprisonment for a further period of one month for the offence under section 451 of the // 2 // Indian Penal Code, to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of seven years and to pay a fine of Rs.7,000/- (rupees seven thousand) and in default, to undergo further rigorous imprisonment for a further period of four months for the offence under section 506 (Part-II) of the Indian Penal Code and to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of five years and to pay a fine of Rs.5,000/- (rupees five thousand) and in default, to undergo further rigorous imprisonment for a further period of three months for the offence under section 8 of the POCSO Act and all the substantive sentences were directed to run consecutively by the learned Ad-hoc Addl.
Sessions Judge, Fast Track Special Court (POCSO), Bhubaneswar vide judgment and order dated 26.12.2022 passed in T.R. Case No.1296 of 2018.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that though the petitioner faced trial, inter alia, for commission of offence under section 376-AB of the Indian Penal Code and section 6 of the POCSO Act but the learned trial Court has acquitted him of both the charges.
Learned counsel further submitted that if all the substantive sentences imposed by the learned trial Court is directed to run concurrently then it would be seven years.

Learned counsel further submitted that during trial, the petitioner was in judicial custody for three years six months and twenty five days which would be evident // 3 // from the accused detail furnished in the second page of the impugned judgment and after pronouncement of the judgment, he has remained in custody for six months more and as such he has already undergone four years of substantive sentence and since there is no chance of early hearing of the appeal in the near future and balance of convenience is in his favour, the bail application may be favouraly considered.

Learned counsel for the State has produced the written instruction dated 31.03.2023 received from the Inspector in-charge of Chandrasekharpur police station, Bhubaneswar UPD from which it appears that the victim is now living peacefully with her mother and the petitioner has got one criminal antecedent of the year 2015.
The written instruction is taken on record.
Learned counsel also placed the evidence of the victim (P.W.1) and doctor (P.W.7).

Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties, the nature of evidence adduced during trial, the period of detention already undergone by the petitioner in judicial custody and absence of any chance of early hearing of the appeal in the near future, I am inclined to release the petitioner on bail.

Let the appellant-petitioner be released on bail pending disposal of the appeal on furnishing bail bond // 4 // of Rs.50,000/- (rupees fifty thousand) with two solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court with such terms and conditions as the learned Court may deem just and proper.
The I.A. is disposed of.
( S.K. Sahoo) Judge 03.
This is an application for stay of realization of fine.
Heard.
There shall be stay of realization of fine amount imposed on the appellant-petitioner by the learned Ad-hoc Addl.
Sessions Judge, Fast Track Special Court (POCSO), Bhubaneswar vide judgment and order dated 26.12.2022 passed in T.R. Case No.1296 of 2018 pending disposal of the criminal appeal.
The I.A. is disposed of.
Issue urgent certified copy as per Rules.
